more.def: Made up of many different kinds of people or things.
examples: The school has a diverse group of students.
The rain forest is home to diverse plants and animals.
She likes a diverse mix of music.

easy.def: Something that turns your attention away.
examples: The clown was a diversion.
The game was a nice diversion.
We needed a diversion.

more.def: Something that takes attention away or gives fun for a short while; also a changed road for traffic.
examples: The magician used a diversion to hide the coin.
Reading is a pleasant diversion on a rainy day.
The road was closed, so we took a diversion.

easy.def: Lots of different kinds of things.
examples: The park has a diversity of plants.
Our school has diversity.
The pond has a diversity of life.

more.def: A mix of many different kinds of people or things.
examples: There is a great diversity of birds in the rain forest.
Our school celebrates the diversity of its students.
The garden's diversity of flowers attracts many bees.

easy.def: To make something go a different way.
examples: The workers diverted the traffic.
He diverted the water.
Divert the river.

more.def: To make something turn or go in a different direction, or to turn attention away from something.
examples: The workers diverted traffic onto a side street while they fixed the road.
Farmers diverted the stream to water their fields.
The clown's funny hat diverted our attention from the magic trick.

easy.def: To split something into parts.
examples: Divide the cake.
We divided the candy.
The river divides the town.

more.def: To split something into parts or groups, or to do division in math.
examples: Divide the pizza into eight slices.
Ten divided by two is five.
The river divides the town in two.

easy.def: Coming from God, or wonderful.
examples: The song was divine.
The cake tasted divine.
The temple felt divine.

more.def: Having to do with God or a god, or so wonderful that it seems heavenly.
examples: In the story, the king asked for divine help.
The cake tasted absolutely divine.
The singer's voice sounded divine.

easy.def: Splitting a number into equal groups.
examples: We learned division in math.
Division is the opposite of multiplication.
Six divided by two is a division.

more.def: The act of splitting a number into equal parts in math, or of separating something into parts.
examples: In math class we practiced long division.
The division of the cake gave everyone a fair slice.
A fence made a clear division between the two yards.

easy.def: When two married people end their marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce.
A divorce can be hard.
Her parents had a divorce.

more.def: The legal ending of a marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce last year.
A divorce can be hard for a family.
The judge granted the divorce.

easy.def: To tell a secret.
examples: Do not divulge the secret.
She divulged the news.
He divulged nothing.

more.def: To tell something that was meant to be secret.
examples: She promised not to divulge the surprise.
He would not divulge where the treasure was hidden.
The spy refused to divulge the plan.

easy.def: To share out.
examples: Let's divvy the candy.
They divvied up the pizza.
Divvy it up.

more.def: To divide something into shares, used in casual talk.
examples: Let's divvy up the pizza.
They divvied the prize among the team.
We divvied the chores among us.

easy.def: The feeling that everything is spinning.
examples: I felt dizziness.
Spinning gives dizziness.
The dizziness went away.

more.def: A feeling that you are spinning or about to fall.
examples: I felt a little dizziness after spinning in circles.
The dizziness went away when I sat down.
The ride gave me a moment of dizziness.

easy.def: Feeling like the room is spinning.
examples: I feel dizzy.
The ride made me dizzy.
I spun around and got dizzy.

more.def: Feeling unsteady, as if everything is spinning around you.
examples: I felt dizzy after spinning in circles.
The roller coaster made her dizzy.
He sat down because he felt dizzy.
